newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan steelmakers 97/98 spending seen at 10-yr low.
newsitem.headline: Japan steelmakers 97/98 spending seen at 10-yr low.

text.p: Combined capital investment at Japan's five major steelmakers this business year will fall to the lowest level in 10 years as they do not plan to launch any large projects.
Overall investment by the major five steelmakers will total 353 billion yen in 1997/98, down from 419 billion a year earlier, according to their plans announced on Tuesday.
The previous record low was the amount of 387.8 billion yen recorded in 1988/89, the Japan Iron and Steel Federation said.
Kawasaki Steel Corp said on Tuesday it plans parent company capital investment of 45 billion yen in 1997/98, down 23.7 percent from an estimated 59 billion yen in 1996/97.
Most companies will use their 1997/98 investment for rationalisation and energy conservation.

Nippon Steel Corp said on Monday it plans parent capital investment of 95 billion yen in 1997/98, down five percent from a year earlier, the lowest since 1970 when Nippon Steel was formed as a result of a merger between Yawata Iron and Steel Co Ltd and Fuji Iron and Steel Co Ltd. The previous record low was 100 billion yen in 1996/97.
Nippon Steel also said it did not carry out fresh spending to boost steel output capacity in 1996/97 and had no plans for such investment in 1997/98.
